transcript.user: Good morning. I am new to crypto and my son told me to look at this. Is my money safe here?
transcript.content:
Good morning, and welcome. Let me answer your question plainly.

Here is what I can tell you about safety. Your money in the MoonSafe vault can only be withdrawn by your own wallet. MoonSafe never holds your keys and cannot move your money. The vault pays no interest and holds only USDC.

The other side matters too. Your wallet is the only key, and there is no second step to confirm a withdrawal today. Anyone who gets your wallet's key or seed phrase can take the whole fund at once, and nobody can reverse it. So guard your seed phrase and never share it with anyone, including people who say they are from support.

A second layer of protection is planned, where your wallet and your email would both be needed, but it is not built yet and has no date.

transcript.user: If somebody steals my wallet can they take my emergency fund? Do you have some kind of two factor?
transcript.content:
Yes, if someone gets your wallet's key or seed phrase, they can take the whole emergency fund in one move, to any address, and nobody can reverse it. MoonSafe cannot stop that or get the money back.

No, there is no two-factor protection today. Your wallet is the only key. A two-key design, where your wallet and your email are both needed, is planned but not built and has no date.

What you can do now is keep your seed phrase offline, write it down on paper, never type it into a website or app, and never share it, even with someone who says they are from support.

transcript.user: What if MoonSafe shuts down, can I still get my money? And can you see or move my money?
transcript.content: Yes, you can still get your money. MoonSafe cannot see your secret keys and cannot move your money. Your fund sits in a vault on the blockchain, and only your wallet can withdraw from it. If MoonSafe shut down, the vault would stay where it is, and you could withdraw directly from the contract with your wallet.

Not by default. Money in your bank account is spare money. MoonSafe does not track it, and it only becomes Safety if you decide to set some aside for that purpose.

transcript.user: So what is the difference between Safety and the emergency fund? Can I use Safety in an emergency?
transcript.content:
Safety and the emergency fund do different jobs.

The emergency fund is for sudden trouble, like losing your income. It is USDC in your MoonSafe vault, sized in months of your spending, so it is ready the moment you need it.

Safety is the steady, low-risk part of your savings. Its job is to keep your whole picture steadier when stocks or crypto fall. A term deposit is locked until it matures, so it is not your emergency money.

So in an emergency, use the emergency fund first. Your $50,000 Safety can help with bigger, planned costs, but it may not be quick to reach, depending on how you hold it.
